Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (pullback by η_{x,λ}); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), chapter-06.txt lines 405–418).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). By the Contract definition of blowUp, for T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) we have η_#T(ω) = T(ν), where ν ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has underlying form ν(y) = ω(−λ⁻¹x + L y) ∘ L with L := λ⁻¹·id (= dilationCLM P λ), i.e. ν(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm L (−λ⁻¹x) ω; it is a test form in η⁻¹(η(U)) and is regarded as a test form in U through the inclusion η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U, which does not change the underlying form).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι. Indeed η is the composition of y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) with the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, and η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z, ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Both η and ι are affine, hence C^∞. In particular η is injective, so η⁻¹(η(V)) = V for every V ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Two facts about supports. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be continuous and f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P). (i) tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f): the set h⁻¹(tsupport f) is closed and contains {f∘h ≠ 0} = h⁻¹{f ≠ 0}. (ii) If h is a homeomorphism and f has compact support, then f∘h has compact support: h⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact (it is the image of the compact set tsupport f under the continuous inverse of h), and tsupport(f∘h) is a closed subset of it by (i).
3. Proof of (a). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and put ω' := ω∘η. Then ω' is C^∞ (composition of C^∞ maps), has compact support by 2(ii), and tsupport ω' ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U by 2(i) and step 1. Hence ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y by definition.
4. Proof of (b). Let ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and put ω := ω'∘ι. Then ω is C^∞, has compact support by 2(ii) (ι is a homeomorphism), and tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω') ⊆ ι⁻¹(U). If ι(z) ∈ U then z = η(ι(z)) ∈ η(U); hence tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Finally ω(η(y)) = ω'(ι(η(y))) = ω'(y) for every y.
5. Proof of (c). Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, and let ν be the test form in the definition of η_#T(ω). Note −λ⁻¹x + L y = η(y). Fix y and v₁,…,vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and put α := ω(η(y)) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P). Since α is multilinear, α(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = (∏_{i=1}^{n} λ⁻¹)·α(v₁,…,vₙ) = λ^{−n}·α(v₁,…,vₙ) (for n = 0 the empty product is 1 = λ⁰). Hence ν(y) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) for all y, so ν = λ^{−n}ω' as elements of 𝒟ⁿ(U). By linearity of T, η_#T(ω) = T(ν) = T(λ^{−n}ω') = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). This proves (a), (b), (c) for arbitrary U and n. ∎

Source. Step 7 of the supplied proof of the selected node (the mass bound (H4)), Simon 7.5.3 and 7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901). Departure: step 6 of the supplied proof (ball(0, R) ⊆ η_i(U) for large i) is replaced by a case distinction on the support of ω. So neither openness of U nor x ∈ U is needed. Sibling used: testform_corr (Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr), parts (a) and (c).

Notation. η_i := η_{x_i,λ_i} = dilation x_i λ_i, so η_i(z) = −λ_i⁻¹x_i + λ_i⁻¹z = λ_i⁻¹(z − x_i). S_i := blowUp T x_i λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(η_i(U)). For an ambient n-form ω, currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(⟨ω, h⟩) if h : (ω is C^∞ with compact support) ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U) holds, and 0 otherwise (Contract definition). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. (Constants.) Take C and r₀ > 0 from the hypothesis and fix R > 0. Put c := max(C, 0)·R^n. Then c ≥ 0.
2. (Large indices.) Since x_i → x, x_i ∈ ball(x, r₀) for all large i. Since λ_iR → 0·R = 0 < r₀, λ_iR < r₀ for all large i. Fix i with both properties and an n-form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R) and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. As λ_i > 0 and R > 0, 0 < λ_iR < r₀.
3. (Case tsupport ω ⊄ η_i(U).) The condition in the definition of currentEval fails, so currentEval(S_i)(ω) = 0 ≤ c.
4. (Case tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U).) Then ω is a test form in η_i(U); write ω̃ ∈ 𝒟^n(η_i(U)) for it (same underlying form). By definition currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω̃). By testform_corr (a) (with P, n, U, x := x_i, λ := λ_i > 0) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with ω'(z) = ω(η_i(z)) for all z ∈ ℝ^P. By testform_corr (c) (with T, ω̃, ω'), S_i(ω̃) = (λ_i⁻¹)^n·T(ω').
5. (Support of ω'.) As functions ω' = ω∘η_i. The affine map η_i is continuous, so tsupport(ω∘η_i) ⊆ η_i⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_comp_subset_preimage) ⊆ η_i⁻¹(ball(0, R)). For z ∈ ℝ^P, |η_i(z)| = λ_i⁻¹|z − x_i|, so η_i(z) ∈ ball(0, R) iff |z − x_i| < λ_iR. Hence tsupport ω' ⊆ ball(x_i, λ_iR).
6. (Admissibility and the mass hypothesis.) For every z, |ω'(z)| = |ω(η_i(z))| ≤ 1. With step 5, ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n (ball(x_i, λ_iR)). GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ofReal(T(ω')) ≤ T.massOn(ball(x_i, λ_iR)). The hypothesis with y := x_i ∈ ball(x, r₀) and ρ := λ_iR ∈ (0, r₀) gives T.massOn(ball(x_i, λ_iR)) ≤ ofReal(C(λ_iR)^n). Hence ofReal(T(ω')) ≤ ofReal(C(λ_iR)^n).
7. (Real bound.) By ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff', T(ω') ≤ C(λ_iR)^n or T(ω') ≤ 0. Since (λ_iR)^n ≥ 0, both C(λ_iR)^n and 0 are ≤ max(C, 0)(λ_iR)^n. So T(ω') ≤ max(C, 0)·(λ_iR)^n.
8. (Conclusion.) Since (λ_i⁻¹)^n > 0 and (λ_i⁻¹)^n(λ_iR)^n = (λ_i⁻¹λ_iR)^n = R^n,
 currentEval(S_i)(ω) = (λ_i⁻¹)^n·T(ω') ≤ (λ_i⁻¹)^n·max(C, 0)·(λ_iR)^n = max(C, 0)·R^n = c.
Steps 3 and 8 give currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c for all large i and all such ω, with c independent of i and ω. ∎

Source. Steps 2–5 of the supplied proof of the selected node (rescaled graphs, bounded offsets, the offset b, C¹ convergence), abstracted from the graph chart; Simon 7.5.5, where the rescaled sheets of N flatten to the tangent plane (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901). Departure: the mean value inequality is applied to u on small balls instead of to g_i. After the substitution v = s_i + λ_iw this is the same estimate.

Notation. B_r := ball(0, r) ⊆ ℝ^m, Du := fderiv ℝ u, ‖·‖ the operator norm, |·| the Euclidean norm.

1. (Regularity of u.) B_δ is open and u is C¹ on it. So u is differentiable at every v ∈ B_δ (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0, then DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt with IsOpen.mem_nhds). Du is continuous on B_δ (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), in particular at 0 ∈ B_δ (δ > 0), where Du(0) = 0.
2. (Small derivative and Lipschitz bound near 0.) Claim: for every η > 0 there is ρ with 0 < ρ ≤ δ such that ‖Du(v)‖ < η for all v ∈ B_ρ, and |u(v') − u(v)| ≤ η|v' − v| for all v, v' ∈ B_ρ. Proof: by step 1 there is ρ₀ > 0 with ‖Du(v)‖ = ‖Du(v) − Du(0)‖ < η whenever |v| < ρ₀. Take ρ := min(ρ₀, δ). Then B_ρ ⊆ B_δ, so u is differentiable on the convex set B_ρ with ‖Du‖ ≤ η there. The mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le with convex_ball) gives the Lipschitz bound.
3. (Chain rule.) Let i ∈ ℕ and w ∈ ℝ^m with s_i + λ_iw ∈ B_δ. The map w ↦ s_i + λ_iw has derivative λ_i·id, and u has derivative Du(s_i + λ_iw) at s_i + λ_iw (step 1). So w ↦ λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i) has derivative λ_i^{−1}·(Du(s_i + λ_iw)∘(λ_i·id)) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) at w, because λ_i ≠ 0. Thus g_i is differentiable at w and Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw).
4. (Ball estimate.) Let i ∈ ℕ, R, r ∈ ℝ and w ∈ ℝ^m with |w| ≤ R and |s_i| + λ_iR < r. Then |s_i + λ_iw| ≤ |s_i| + λ_i|w| ≤ |s_i| + λ_iR < r, so s_i + λ_iw ∈ B_r. Moreover, for every c ∈ ℝ, |s_i| + λ_ic → 0 + 0·c = 0.
5. (C₀ ≥ 0.) The filter atTop on ℕ is proper, so the hypothesis holds for at least one index i. The corresponding w satisfies 0 ≤ |w| ≤ C₀.
6. (g_i(0) is bounded.) Take ρ₁ ∈ (0, δ] from step 2 with η = 1. By the hypothesis and step 4 (c = C₀) there is i₂ such that every i ≥ i₂ has a point w_i with |w_i| ≤ C₀, s_i + λ_iw_i ∈ B_δ and |u(s_i + λ_iw_i) − t_i| ≤ C₀λ_i, and moreover |s_i| + λ_iC₀ < ρ₁. Fix such i. Step 4 gives s_i ∈ B_{ρ₁} (take w = 0; this uses C₀ ≥ 0) and s_i + λ_iw_i ∈ B_{ρ₁}. The Lipschitz bound of step 2 gives |u(s_i) − u(s_i + λ_iw_i)| ≤ λ_i|w_i| ≤ λ_iC₀. Hence |u(s_i) − t_i| ≤ λ_iC₀ + C₀λ_i = 2C₀λ_i and |g_i(0)| = λ_i^{−1}|u(s_i) − t_i| ≤ 2C₀. So g_{i₂+j}(0) ∈ closedBall(0, 2C₀) ⊆ ℝ^k for every j ∈ ℕ.
7. (The subsequence and b.) closedBall(0, 2C₀) is compact (isCompact_closedBall). IsCompact.tendsto_subseq gives b ∈ ℝ^k and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with g_{i₂+φ(j)}(0) → b. Put σ(j) := i₂ + φ(j). Then σ is strictly increasing and g_{σ(j)}(0) → b. Also σ(j) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), so for every c ∈ ℝ, |s_{σ(j)}| + λ_{σ(j)}c → 0 (step 4 composed with σ).
8. ((H1).) Let R > 0. By step 7, |s_{σ(j)}| + λ_{σ(j)}R < δ for all large j. For such j and w ∈ B_R, step 4 gives s_{σ(j)} + λ_{σ(j)}w ∈ B_δ, and by step 3 g_{σ(j)} is differentiable at w.
9. ((H2).) Let R > 0 and ε > 0. Put η := min(ε, ε/(2R)) > 0; then ηR ≤ (ε/(2R))·R = ε/2. Take ρ ∈ (0, δ] from step 2 for this η. By step 7, for all large j both |s_{σ(j)}| + λ_{σ(j)}R < ρ and |g_{σ(j)}(0) − b| < ε/2 hold. Fix such j and write s := s_{σ(j)}, λ := λ_{σ(j)}, g := g_{σ(j)}. Let w ∈ B_R. By step 4, s + λw ∈ B_ρ ⊆ B_δ, and s ∈ B_ρ (take w = 0 there, using R > 0).
 (a) Derivative: by step 3, Dg(w) = Du(s + λw), so ‖Dg(w)‖ < η ≤ ε by step 2.
 (b) Values: g(w) − g(0) = λ^{−1}(u(s + λw) − u(s)). The Lipschitz bound gives |g(w) − g(0)| ≤ λ^{−1}·η·|λw| = η|w| ≤ ηR ≤ ε/2. Hence |g(w) − b| ≤ |g(w) − g(0)| + |g(0) − b| < ε/2 + ε/2 = ε.
Steps 7–9 give σ and b with all the stated properties. ∎

Chain rule: g_i is differentiable at w with Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) whenever s_i + λ_iw ∈ B_δ.
The offsets and the 1-Lipschitz bound give |g_i(0)| ≤ 2C₀ for i ≥ i₂. Compactness of closedBall(0, 2C₀) gives σ(j) = i₂ + φ(j) and b with g_{σ(j)}(0) → b.
For w ∈ B_R and large j, s + λw lies in B_ρ: (H1) by the chain rule; (H2) from ‖Du‖ < η and |g(w) − g(0)| ≤ η|w| ≤ ε/2.

Source. Step 1 and the first half of step 3 of the supplied proof of the selected node (coordinates of the centres; nearby carrier points lie on the graph and have bounded offsets), Simon 7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901). Departure: |p_i − x| is bounded by |C₀|λ_i + |x_i − x|, so the sign of C₀ needs no separate treatment.

1. (Pythagoras.) For a ∈ ℝ^m and b ∈ ℝ^k, |ιa + ι'b|² = |ιa|² + 2⟨ιa, ι'b⟩ + |ι'b|² = |a|² + |b|² (norm_add_sq_real, orthogonality, and LinearIsometry.norm_map). Hence |a| ≤ |ιa + ι'b| and |b| ≤ |ιa + ι'b|.
2. (Coordinates of the centres.) For each i choose s_i, t_i with x_i − x = ιs_i + ι't_i (spanning hypothesis applied to x_i − x). Then x_i = x + ιs_i + ι't_i. By step 1, |s_i| ≤ |x_i − x| and |t_i| ≤ |x_i − x|, and |x_i − x| → 0, so s_i → 0 and t_i → 0 by the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm).
3. (Nearby carrier points converge to x.) For each i choose p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i. Since λ_i > 0, C₀λ_i ≤ |C₀|λ_i. Hence |p_i − x| ≤ |p_i − x_i| + |x_i − x| ≤ |C₀|λ_i + |x_i − x| → |C₀|·0 + 0 = 0. So |p_i − x| < min(δ₁, δ₂) for all sufficiently large i.
4. (p_i lies on the graph.) Fix such an i. Choose a, b with p_i − x = ιa + ι'b. By step 1, |a| ≤ |p_i − x| < δ₁ and |b| ≤ |p_i − x| < δ₂. Hence p_i = x + ιa + ι'b ∈ {x + ιv + ι'w : |v| < δ₁, |w| < δ₂}, and p_i ∈ N. By the chart identity there is v with |v| < δ₁ and p_i = x + ιv + ι'u(v).
5. (The offset w.) Put w := λ_i^{−1}(v − s_i). Then s_i + λ_iw = v ∈ ball(0, δ₁). By step 2 and linearity, p_i − x_i = (x + ιv + ι'u(v)) − (x + ιs_i + ι't_i) = ι(v − s_i) + ι'(u(v) − t_i). By step 1, |v − s_i| ≤ |p_i − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i and |u(v) − t_i| ≤ |p_i − x_i| ≤ C₀λ_i. Therefore |w| = λ_i^{−1}|v − s_i| ≤ C₀, and |u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i| = |u(v) − t_i| ≤ C₀λ_i.
Steps 2–5 give the sequences s and t and, for every sufficiently large i, the required w. ∎
